data.title: Apple Begins Global iPhone 18 Pro Sales as AI Features Face Regional Limits
data.description:
Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL) began global sales of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max on Friday, September 18, turning the company's latest flagship announcement into its first broad commercial rollout. Apple also released the Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and AirPods 5 in stores and online.

In a September 18 newsroom update, Apple said the products were available through its retail locations, website and Apple Store app. The company described customers trying the devices and receiving setup and trade-in assistance, but it did not report unit sales, order volumes or revenue from the launch.

The iPhone 18 Pro models combine Apple's A20 Pro chip with a 48-megapixel Fusion Main camera and variable aperture, according to the original product announcement. Apple is presenting the phones as a mix of hardware and artificial-intelligence upgrades, with iOS 27, Apple Intelligence and a new Siri AI experience among the features highlighted for supported markets.

That software story is not uniform worldwide. Apple said Siri AI will not be available initially in the European Union, citing the need to find a path that preserves privacy and security. The limitation does not establish a financial impact, but it gives investors a concrete regional difference to watch as the new devices move through their first sales cycle.

Launch-day operations also faced a localized labor dispute. Reuters reported that unions representing more than 1,600 employees at 17 Italian Apple stores staged a one-day strike over working conditions. Apple said its retail and online stores remained open, and the report provided no evidence of a material interruption to global sales.

For shareholders, Friday's event supplies a new data point but not a demand verdict. Opening-day queues and company photographs are not a substitute for order trends, shipment timing or reported revenue. The next useful evidence will come from lead times, carrier and trade-in activity, and Apple's results. Reuters also reported that Apple's first foldable smartphone, the Duo, is scheduled to reach the market on October 23, creating another near-term product milestone.

data.title: Nucor Guides to Higher Q3 Profit, but Below Analysts' Estimate
data.description:
Nucor Corporation (NYSE: NUE) expects third-quarter 2026 earnings of $5.55 to $5.65 per diluted share, the steelmaker said on September 17 after the market close. The range is above Nucor's $5.04 per-share result in the second quarter and $2.63 in the third quarter of 2025, but below the $5.89 analyst estimate cited by Reuters.

The outlook points to stronger earnings in Nucor's steel mills and steel products segments compared with the second quarter. The company expects higher average selling prices and stable volumes in steel mills, while steel products should benefit from both higher volumes and higher realized pricing. Nucor expects the raw materials segment to contribute less because of lower pricing and shipments.

That mix is important because the second quarter included a $130 million cash benefit from refunds tied to earlier raw-material procurement costs. Nucor said it does not expect a similar benefit in the third quarter. The company also recorded a $61 million non-cash, pre-tax gain from a higher valuation of its investment in Helion, a fusion-energy company. The absence of that gain is expected to increase corporate and elimination expenses in the coming quarter.

The market's initial response was cautious. Reuters reported that Nucor shares were down 2% in premarket trading on September 18 at $260.37, while Steel Dynamics also fell after issuing a below-consensus third-quarter outlook. The reaction suggests investors were weighing the expected year-over-year profit growth against the gap between Nucor's guidance and current expectations.

For stock-market readers, the release offers a more mixed signal than the headline earnings growth implies. Pricing and volumes are improving in Nucor's core steel operations, but the comparison with the prior quarter is affected by one-time benefits and weaker raw-material economics. Nucor plans to report third-quarter results after the close on October 26 and hold its earnings call the following morning.

Source: Nucor's third-quarter guidance release.

data.title: Warren Buffett Leaves Berkshire Chair as Howard Buffett Takes Board Lead
data.description:
Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK-B) completed another stage of its leadership transition on September 18. Warren Buffett became chairman emeritus with immediate effect, while his son Howard G. Buffett was elected chairman of the board. Warren Buffett will remain a director, keeping him formally involved after more than six decades at the company.

The company's announcement also leaves Susan Decker in place as lead independent director. Howard Buffett has served on Berkshire's board since 1993. The company described his appointment as part of its long-standing succession plan, rather than a change in operating control.

That distinction matters because Greg Abel remains chief executive and continues to run Berkshire's businesses. Warren Buffett's attached shareholder letter said Abel has already taken full command of the CEO role and that the new chair will focus on preserving the company's culture and values. The arrangement separates day-to-day management from the board chairmanship while retaining Warren Buffett's judgment at the director level.

The development is separate from the CEO succession announced in May 2025 and completed at the start of 2026. That earlier step transferred executive responsibility to Abel while Warren Buffett stayed chairman. Friday's action now moves the board's top role to Howard Buffett, making the division of responsibilities among Abel, Howard Buffett and Warren Buffett more explicit.

The Associated Press reported that Warren Buffett had held the chairmanship since 1970 after taking control of the former textile company in 1965. Over that period, Berkshire became a broad conglomerate spanning insurance, freight rail, utilities and energy, manufacturing, services and retailing. Howard Buffett brings 33 years of experience on Berkshire's board, while Abel previously oversaw its non-insurance operations.

For shareholders, the immediate change is one of governance rather than operating strategy. Abel remains responsible for capital allocation and business performance, Howard Buffett assumes leadership of the board, and Warren Buffett retains a director's seat. The structure provides continuity, but it also puts the post-Buffett division of authority into practice more fully than the earlier CEO handoff alone.

data.title: Amazon and Walmart Face FTC Probe Request Over AI Shopping and U.S.-Made Claims
data.description:
Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) and Walmart (NASDAQ: WMT) face a bipartisan request for federal scrutiny of their AI shopping assistants after senators questioned how the tools handle American-made products. The September 17 request adds a consumer-protection issue to the retailers' use of AI to guide purchases, but does not itself establish that a new investigation has begun.

Senators Tammy Baldwin and Rick Scott asked the Federal Trade Commission to investigate whether Amazon's Alexa for Shopping and Walmart's Sparky suppress information about products made in the United States and fail to flag potentially false origin labels. Their letter cites research suggesting that the assistants can identify country-of-origin information and suspicious claims, yet do not consistently make that information available to shoppers.

The allegations remain contested. Amazon told Reuters that it does not intentionally withhold country-of-origin information. The company said Alexa for Shopping is still improving and currently directs customers asking about origin to product detail pages to prioritize accuracy. The FTC declined to comment, and Walmart had not immediately responded to Reuters' request for comment when the report was updated on September 17.

The labeling issue predates the current AI dispute. In July 2025, the FTC sent letters to both retailers identifying third-party sellers whose U.S.-origin claims appeared potentially deceptive. The agency said an unqualified Made in USA claim requires a product to be all or virtually all made domestically. It urged the marketplaces to address misleading claims under their seller policies.

That history does not amount to a finding against Walmart. The FTC's 2025 letter to the company explicitly said it was not assessing whether Walmart itself had violated the relevant law or labeling rule. The new senators' request instead seeks scrutiny of how AI assistants present product information and how retailers monitor questionable listings.

For shareholders, the issue is whether AI shopping features create additional compliance work alongside their commercial promise. If the FTC pursues the concerns and requires changes, product recommendations and seller-monitoring processes could need revisions. The reported request supplies no estimate of financial exposure, and the available evidence does not establish a resulting penalty or earnings impact.

data.title: SEC Opens Five-Year Path for Tokenized Stock Trading, With Limits
data.description:
The Securities and Exchange Commission opened a five-year regulatory path for tokenized stock trading on September 17, giving qualifying platforms a way to trade blockchain-based shares under a temporary set of conditions. The decision advances an experiment that could change how stocks move between buyers and sellers, while preserving key shareholder protections.

The SEC's Innovation Exemption covers permissioned venues using automated market makers and liquidity pools, which allow participants to trade against pooled assets. Eligible venues receive relief from the legal definition of an exchange, while qualifying liquidity providers receive a separate dealer exemption. The framework also limits the number of securities and trading volume, and requires trading to stop when the underlying stock is halted on its primary exchange.

For investors, a central condition concerns what they actually own. Under the SEC order, eligible tokens must carry the same rights as the equivalent class of conventional shares, including dividends and voting rights. Synthetic products that merely provide exposure to a stock through derivatives fall outside the exemption. The relief applies to secondary trading, rather than initial offerings of securities.

Companies also have a say when an unaffiliated third party tokenizes their shares. A venue must give the underlying issuer written notice and wait at least 30 calendar days after receipt before offering those tokens for trading. An objection within that window prevents the venue from making them available. That gives issuers a concrete check on third-party listings under this framework.

The commercial appeal is broader access and faster processing. Reuters reported that industry advocates see tokenization as a route to round-the-clock trading, immediate settlement and lower transaction costs. Those are potential benefits, rather than results demonstrated by the new exemption. Adoption and liquidity will determine how useful the permitted venues become.

Commissioner Hester Peirce described the measure as an interim experiment intended to help the SEC understand how blockchain-based trading interacts with traditional markets before developing a more durable framework. For the stock market, the immediate change is a defined route to test a different trading model; the longer-term competitive impact remains to be established.

data.title: What’s Ahead for the Stock Market This Week
data.description:
After Friday’s sharp selloff triggered by President Trump’s decision to raise tariffs in response to China tightening rare earth exports, investors are starting the week on edge. The focus now shifts to trade tensions, earnings season, and the Federal Reserve’s next moves.

Big Earnings Week: Banks and Chipmakers Take Center Stage

This week kicks off a busy stretch of third-quarter results from major financial firms and tech companies.

  • Banks: JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Citigroup all report on Tuesday, followed by Bank of America and Morgan Stanley on Wednesday. Later in the week, American Express, Truist Financial, and State Street will wrap up the financial lineup.
  • Tech & Chips: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) reports Thursday after strong AI chip sales boosted its revenue 40% in the first half of 2025. ASML follows on Wednesday after raising concerns about tariffs and slowing demand for chip equipment.
  • Tech events: Oracle’s AI World conference begins Monday, and Salesforce’s Dreamforce starts Tuesday — both likely to bring attention to artificial intelligence and enterprise tech. Earnings Calendar >>

Data Delays and Fed Watch

The federal government shutdown, now entering its third week, is likely to delay several key reports, including retail sales, inflation (PPI), housing starts, and jobless claims. Some data will still come through, like the NFIB Small Business Optimism Index on Tuesday and homebuilder confidence on Thursday.

Investors will also tune in to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s speech on Tuesday, along with comments from Fed officials, including Michelle Bowman and Christopher Waller. The Fed’s Beige Book, which gives an overview of economic conditions across regions, will be released on Wednesday.

Market Context

Bond markets will be closed on Monday for Columbus Day (also observed as Indigenous Peoples Day), but stock exchanges will remain open.

With limited economic data and uncertainty around Washington’s budget standoff, markets are likely to take their cues from corporate earnings and Fed commentary.

In short, this week is about navigating through noise — balancing worries over tariffs and the shutdown against potential optimism from strong bank and chipmaker earnings.

data.title: What Is the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA)? A Complete Guide
data.description:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA), often referred to as the Dow Jones, the Dow 30, or simply the Dow, is one of the world’s most recognized stock market indexes. The DJIA tracks 30 of the largest publicly traded companies in the United States, making it a widely followed indicator of the overall health of the U.S. economy and stock market. Investors searching for DJIA today, DJIA futures, or Dow Jones price updates often turn to this index as a barometer of market sentiment.

But what exactly is the DJIA, what stocks does it include, and how do traders and long-term investors use it in their strategies?

What Is the DJIA?

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) is a price-weighted index created in 1896 by Charles Dow and Edward Jones. Unlike market-cap-weighted indexes like the S&P 500, the DJIA assigns weight based on a stock’s price rather than its market capitalization. This means a company with a higher stock price (e.g., Apple or UnitedHealth) influences the index more heavily than lower-priced stocks.

The DJIA is designed to reflect the performance of blue-chip companies across different sectors of the U.S. economy. It does not include utilities or transportation stocks, which are tracked by separate Dow indexes.

What Companies Are in the DJIA?

The DJIA is composed of 30 large, publicly traded U.S. companies that are considered leaders in their industries. These companies span sectors such as technology, finance, healthcare, consumer goods, and industrials.

Here’s a snapshot of the DJIA holdings (as of 2025, September 15th):

How Does the DJIA Work?

  • Price-Weighted Methodology: Higher-priced stocks have more influence.
  • Dow Divisor: A proprietary number adjusted for stock splits, dividends, and corporate actions ensures continuity.
  • Sector Balance: While tech stocks (Apple, Microsoft) now hold significant weight, the index aims to represent the broader U.S. economy.

If Apple (AAPL) rises $5 in a day, it has the same impact on the DJIA as Boeing (BA) rising $5, even though their market caps differ drastically.

Why Do Investors Watch the DJIA?

  • Economic Barometer: The DJIA today is seen as a snapshot of the U.S. economy.
  • Historical Importance: Created in 1896, it has over 125 years of market history.
  • Market Sentiment: Widely quoted on news outlets and financial platforms.
  • Trading Opportunities: Investors follow DJIA futures, DJIA ETFs, and Dow Jones index funds for exposure.

How to Trade or Invest in the DJIA

Investors can’t buy the DJIA directly but can gain exposure through exchange-traded funds (ETFs), futures contracts, or mutual funds:

  • SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) – tracks the DJIA closely.
  • DJIA Futures – contracts traded on CME, allowing leveraged exposure.
  • Index Funds – designed for long-term buy-and-hold investors.

data.title: Bank of Japan Raises Rate to 1.25%, Leaves Next Hike Timing Open
data.description:
The Bank of Japan voted on September 18 to raise its short-term policy rate from 1.00% to 1.25%, extending the shift toward higher borrowing costs across major economies. The quarter-point increase was widely expected, but the split vote and Governor Kazuo Ueda's comments left the timing of further moves open.

The official decision passed 7–2 and takes effect on September 24. It targets the uncollateralized overnight call rate. The rate paid on eligible balances held at the central bank will also rise to 1.25%, while its basic lending rate will become 1.50%.

The BOJ said underlying consumer inflation was approaching its 2% target and warned of an overshoot. It cited expensive oil, yen depreciation and rising wages among the sources of price pressure. Yet it still expects financial conditions to support economic activity after the increase, distinguishing this adjustment from a declaration that credit has become restrictive.

No fixed timetable for the next increase

At his subsequent news conference, Ueda said the bank had no preset schedule, such as raising rates every three months, according to Reuters' translated account. He also said the level of the neutral rate, and therefore the eventual stopping point for increases, was difficult to identify. The central bank will assess policy at each meeting.

Reuters reported that the increase took rates to their highest level in 31 years, but the yen weakened as investors focused on the absence of more aggressive guidance and the two dissenting votes. That reaction underscores the distinction between an anticipated decision and fresh information about what comes next.

The BOJ's statement commits to further increases as economic activity, prices and financial conditions warrant, while the dissenters questioned the case for acting now. For global equity investors, the decision adds another source of changing financing conditions. Higher yen borrowing costs can alter the economics of investments funded in Japan, while currency movements affect the dollar value of Japanese holdings. Neither channel establishes a uniform outcome for U.S. stocks; the future pace of tightening remains central to the significance of this move.

data.title: U.S. Jobless Claims Fall to 196,000 After Fed Rate Hike
data.description:
U.S. applications for unemployment benefits fell to 196,000 in the week ended September 12, adding a fresh sign of limited layoffs a day after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates. The September 17 release points to continued labor-market resilience, although holiday-related volatility complicates the weekly comparison.

The Labor Department's report, released at 8:30 a.m. Eastern, showed seasonally adjusted initial claims declined by 10,000 from an unrevised 206,000. The four-week average, which reduces the influence of a single week's movement, fell by 2,750 to 203,250.

Continuing claims also declined. The number receiving benefits after an initial week of aid fell by 39,000 to 1.730 million for the week ended September 5. That series covers an earlier week than the headline initial-claims figure. Its previous reading was revised down by 5,000 to 1.769 million.

Holiday effects temper the signal

Reuters reported that economists had expected 208,000 initial claims. It cautioned that the surprise decline likely reflected volatility around Labor Day, when seasonal adjustments can be difficult. The report also noted that low layoffs are doing much of the work in supporting labor-market stability, while employers remain cautious about hiring. Fewer benefit applications therefore do not establish a broad acceleration in recruitment.

The data arrive after the Fed's September 16 decision to lift its target range by a quarter percentage point to 3.75%–4.00%. Policymakers described solid economic growth and resilient spending but said inflation remained elevated. StockInvest's coverage of that decision details the policy backdrop; Thursday's claims report supplies a new labor-market observation rather than a change in the Fed's announced position.

For stocks, the combination presents competing implications. Limited layoffs can help sustain household income and demand, while persistent economic strength can leave policymakers less urgency to lower borrowing costs. This single, holiday-sensitive release does not settle that balance or measure the effect of a rate increase announced only the day before.

data.title: Snap Pitches $2,195 Specs Glasses to Businesses With New AI Partnerships
data.description:
Snap (NYSE: SNAP) used its September 16 Specs launch to pitch its $2,195 augmented-reality glasses as both a consumer device and a workplace computer. New enterprise partnerships broaden the sales proposition beyond entertainment, with applications aimed at retail staff, field-service teams and remote support.

Yahoo Finance reported that Specs run applications without a separate connected device. Snap had initially revealed the glasses in June; this week's event added detail on their capabilities and the Specs Intelligence AI service. The software is designed to bring relevant information into view and will also be available on Mac and iPhone.

A workplace case for premium-priced glasses

In its enterprise announcement, Snap said Salesforce (NYSE: CRM) is bringing Agentforce to Specs. Planned uses include identifying equipment, creating a service case and updating records while employees remain at the task. Amazon's (NASDAQ: AMZN) AWS is working to connect its Amazon Quick assistant, with retail inventory lookup offered as one example.

Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) is working with Snap on agents built using its XR AI software, intended to interpret a worker's surroundings and retrieve company information. Other partners address remote expert assistance and access to documents or 3D models. Snap also says it is developing device-management and security capabilities for business deployments.

The commercial question is whether those uses justify the hardware cost for employers. The partnerships establish planned integrations, but they do not establish widespread adoption or a predictable revenue contribution. Reuters reported that financial terms were not disclosed and shipping is expected later this fall in the United States, Britain and France. For Snap, workplace applications add another possible customer base while the product's commercial rollout is still ahead.
